CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFIF/CFELSEIF/CFELSE

CFIF evaluates an expression and processes the code up to the next CFELSEIF, CFELSE or /CFIF only if the expression is true. CFELSEIF tests another expression when everything above it was false, and CFELSE catches whatever is left.

Category

Flow control

Syntax

<CFIF expression>
  HTML and CFML
<CFELSEIF expression>
  HTML and CFML
<CFELSE>
  HTML and CFML
</CFIF>

Usage

The expression is written without pound signs. Comparisons use word operators, not symbols:

Operator Also written Meaning
IS EQ, EQUAL equal (strings compare without regard to case)
IS NOT NEQ, NOT EQUAL not equal
GT GREATER THAN greater than
LT LESS THAN less than
GTE GE, GREATER THAN OR EQUAL TO greater than or equal
LTE LE, LESS THAN OR EQUAL TO less than or equal
CONTAINS the string contains the other one
DOES NOT CONTAIN the opposite

Combine tests with AND, OR, NOT, XOR, EQV and IMP, and group them with parentheses. Any value that converts to a boolean works on its own: <CFIF Staff.RecordCount> is true when the query returned rows, and "Yes", "True" and non-zero numbers count as true.

You can have as many CFELSEIF blocks as you like, but only one CFELSE, and it must come last. For long chains of tests against a single value, CFSWITCH is easier to read.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFQUERY NAME="Staff" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets">
SELECT FirstName, LastName, Department, Salary, Contract
FROM Employees WHERE Department IN ('Sales', 'Engineering')
ORDER BY Salary DESC
</CFQUERY>

<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TH>Name</TH><TH>Salary</TH><TH>Band</TH><TH>Notes</TH></TR>
<CFOUTPUT QUERY="Staff">
<TR>
  <TD>#FirstName# #LastName#</TD>
  <TD ALIGN="RIGHT">#DollarFormat(Salary)#</TD>
  <CFIF Salary GTE 75000>
    <TD BGCOLOR="##CCFFCC">Senior</TD>
  <CFELSEIF Salary GTE 55000>
    <TD BGCOLOR="##FFFFCC">Regular</TD>
  <CFELSE>
    <TD BGCOLOR="##FFE0E0">Junior</TD>
  </CFIF>
  <TD><CFIF Contract>Contractor</CFIF><CFIF Department IS "Sales" AND LastName CONTAINS "a"> Sales, with an "a"</CFIF>&nbsp;</TD>
</TR>
</CFOUTPUT>
</TABLE>
